items.source: Standard Astra t9q review of 58eada75f58ff0ec77cf85253e4746488992231f with the pinned Lightweight Charts SDK.
items.observation: While holding a drag from before the first quote, the historical 09:40 wick stayed at x=519.5 on append, then jumped to x=378.5 on the next +6 px move instead of x=525.5. The SDK keeps a scroll-start offset based on the old time-scale base index. At the left limit the reviewer also observed an immediate one-bar shift on the first append. The original task check started holding the drag after the append.

resolution.cause: The SDK updates its base index when the first replay bar appears, while an active scroll retains its captured offset relative to the old base. The first append may also clamp the previously valid left limit before compensating for the new base.
resolution.correction: On explicit Start, reserve the single replay time with an invisible axis-only series and reapply the existing logical range. The first admitted quote fills that slot without advancing the base index. Reset clears the slot and restores the frozen series.
resolution.prevention: The ordinary Chromium entry first reproduced the 147 px jump, then verified a held drag across append and an additional 6 px move, along with a stationary left limit. Independent native X11 crops and Standard Astra narrow review cross-checked the corrected commit.

items.source: Independent t47 review of the 4498ebc private-record repair and subsequent two-window observation at 3bad802.
items.observation: A committed deletion with a lost approval reply lost its receipt recovery control when a later detail read returned DATA_UNAVAILABLE. A pre-commit BUSY followed by a peer rename retained the stale target title while offering Retry. The 4498ebc Chromium baseline reproduced all three cases with actual SQLite responses. The repaired journey recovered the same deletion receipt following a dropped reply and a blocked post-commit checkpoint, kept exactly one tombstone and completed cleanup. A pre-commit BUSY followed by a peer rename kept the old content hidden and rejected the original resolution as stale. The prior six Chromium private-record journeys also passed. Evidence is retained under .reports/private-record-v8/delete-reply-green.

resolution.cause: The refresh path treated a missing detail as cancellation of an approval whose commit result was unknown.
resolution.correction: Retain the original body-free resolution until a matching receipt, a definitive stale result or access denial. Drop superseded displayed content independently.
resolution.prevention: The real browser covers lost reply, committed cleanup BUSY, and pre-commit BUSY with a peer rename. SQLite verifies one tombstone and completed cleanup.

items.source: Independent t47 review of 8c9d27f, recorded in the M2-001 Herdr review terminal.
items.observation: The synthetic two-window fixture retained a deleted memory on writer loss, discarded a local draft on peer correction, and kept a stale deletion review visible after known removal. Reviews omitted record identity. The reviewer identified cross-window cancellation interference and found that restore preview accounts only for current records also in the archive. The unchanged 57a9cab runtime reproduced those findings through the real Chromium and Rust routes. The repair passed six local Chromium lifecycle and review cases and the SQLite persistence suite. Independent confirmation remains pending.

resolution.cause: The panel and approval stage coupled multiple windows and revisions. The restore preview counted only the intersection with archived records.
resolution.correction: Separate draft and displayed data, scope each confirmation, clear known inaccessible content, and count all surviving current records during preview.
resolution.prevention: Two writers exercise connection loss, peer change and deletion. Rust checks independent approvals and restoration with current-only records.

items.source: Independent Herdr review of the M1-006 working implementation and its real local worker and chart probes.
items.observation: A changed bar at the frozen sequence could be ignored, history and replay could reuse a request ID across tasks, and cancellation could keep the next subscription busy. Superseded preparation delayed the new selection. Comparing the whole canvas could pass when the final candle was missing, and a stalled child could retain the caller beyond the configured cleanup budget.

resolution.cause: The initial replay treated all older sequence numbers as harmless and kept separate request ownership paths. The chart, worker lifecycle and test oracle did not independently demonstrate cancellation or the final candle.
resolution.correction: The shared registry checks the frozen boundary, the worker uses one request ledger and cleanup retains ownership of unreaped children. Browser and native preparation can be superseded.
resolution.prevention: The live chart check measures both candle closes, a frozen historical readout and selection races. Rust and Python regressions cover conflicting boundary events, identity reuse and bounded cleanup, including the portable desktop bridge.

items.source: Independent read-only inspection and local synthetic probe while preparing market-quality acceptance.

resolution.cause: The provider derived freshness from a single display label and always rebuilt the normal revision. The combined replay path could also offer a stream boundary without an observation at the cutoff.
resolution.correction: Read the specified fixture revision, compute session, freshness and coverage independently, derive the legacy summary, and require a matching observed cutoff for replay.
resolution.prevention: Worker and frozen-page tests cover closed, delayed, stale and unknown data with gaps, empty selections, pinned revisions and a stale or unknown observation that still has subsequent fixture events.

items.source: Windows hosted verification run 44495516299, check harness after the market-live-stream process returned exit code 1.
items.observation: The Windows console could not encode the browser failure text. The harness stopped before writing its report, so the hosted job lacked a downloadable Windows report for the original failure.

resolution.cause: Printing the raw Unicode tail on a legacy console could raise a second exception before harness finalization.
resolution.correction: Escape the short structured console diagnostic while retaining the original bytes, digest and failing exit status in the check log. Preserve the private-check output boundary.
resolution.prevention: The strict-encoding child-process regression and the private diagnostic test ran locally and on both hosted platforms in run 44498344930. The Windows report, including the successful market replay, was staged and imported. The earlier browser assertion was unavailable in run 44495516299.

items.source: M2-001 implementation planning, product AI tool policy compared with registered protocol 1.1 client and AI selection requests.
items.observation: The generic policy requires a workspace revision for every mutation, but workspace.selectEvidence requires the expected selection revision and explicitly allows selection changes without advancing the durable workspace revision.

resolution.cause: The generic AI tool instruction predated the versioned shared selection and applied one revision rule to different operations.
resolution.correction: The contract now specifies the independent selection revision for a shared selection, the durable workspace revision for a write, and both for a selection-bound write. Existing 1.1 clients keep the registered shapes.
resolution.prevention: Five shared negative vectors exercise omitted and substituted revision fields in human and AI requests. Python, Rust and TypeScript validate the positive and negative cases. Runtime concurrency and projection remain part of M2-001.

items.source: Independent timing review of an owned history preparation and market replay during M1-007.
items.observation: A replacement could stop attempting admission after 1000 ms for preview history or 1550 ms for a replay even though its previous worker was still within the bridge cleanup window. A simulated 1025 ms or 1600 ms release reproduced the two false BUSY results.

resolution.cause: Three admission loops used fixed and inconsistent budgets that could expire before cleanup. A BUSY error delivered inside an already admitted stream could be mistaken for a new admission refusal.
resolution.correction: Use a cancellable monotonic admission window covering worker cleanup. Acknowledge admission on the transport boundary and stop automatic retries once the worker has accepted the operation.
resolution.prevention: Browser regressions delay replacement reads and subscriptions beyond the old limits, hold persistent BUSY and verify only one subscription after a terminal-only BUSY.

items.source: Independent M1-007 chart review with held ordinary history, controlled transport failures and a typed gap event.
items.observation: Without a snapshot, a failed worker read populated the source connection as disconnected. With a frozen snapshot, loss of the local preview transport could instead be presented as a worker exit. The UI also discarded known UTC ranges and loss counts when a stream gap arrived. A validated replay gap can arrive before a later cleanup error. Preserve the reported facts even if the terminal says TIMEOUT or the local transport then disconnects.

resolution.cause: The view conflated source status with worker and local transport failures. It initially associated known loss with the normal terminal rather than the validated gap event.
resolution.correction: Keep source, worker and transport facts independent. Retain accepted gap range, reason and loss immediately across normal completion, cleanup failure or transport loss, and discard the old replay on retry or selection change.
resolution.prevention: The quality suite uses real pinned and unpinned history errors plus controlled transport cases, including a held then failed terminal and rejected post-gap updates. Independent review confirmed the same gap and failure remain visible together.

items.source: Independent M1-007 chart review with held ordinary history, controlled transport failures and a typed gap event.
items.observation: Switching symbols aborted the caller while a superseded ordinary browser history fetch still occupied the read queue until its old response arrived. This left the replacement chart loading while an obsolete response was held.

resolution.cause: Ordinary development-preview reads did not receive the selection abort signal, so an obsolete network response held the client queue.
resolution.correction: Cancel preview reads on replacement while allowing the prior child to be reaped before readmission. Preserve the native invoke boundary and the latest selection identity.
resolution.prevention: The normal chart must paint the replacement stock while the obsolete futures response is still held, confirm cancellation and reject late paints. The native preparation and slot ownership checks remain in the replay suite.

items.source: Independent review of engineering contract 1.4.1 against the committed annotation, receipt identities and EvidenceTarget11.
items.observation: The generic revision check can read as applying to an already committed retry despite the original revision having advanced. The selection description omits the object-ID target family and explicit null clearing supported by both 1.1 callers.

resolution.cause: New-work concurrency wording did not distinguish an already committed semantic retry, and the prose target list omitted legitimate variants from the 1.1 union.
resolution.correction: Scope revision, target and confirmation checks to new work after the committed lookup. Qualify visible receipts and required result fields with current disclosure and data rights. Specify object identity, explicit null clearing and the source locators for the other target forms.
resolution.prevention: Six new human and AI vectors distinguish object selection, explicit clearing and omitted target. All 162 shared vectors passed in Python, TypeScript and Rust. Independent review checked the original annotation request, advanced committed revision and projected result. Process-level idempotency remains an M2-001 runtime check.

items.source: Ubuntu Verify delivery run 44504564860 at edb0189, market-live-stream, first canvas replay.
items.observation: The five-second terminal assertion reached Preparing then In progress before timing out. The other seven replay cases passed. The original log and screenshot are retained in the authenticated run artifact.

resolution.cause: The terminal assertion started at the user action and consumed one five-second budget across two real operations. A held preparation reproduced the hosted in-progress timeout. Later Chromium protocol access could also lose an already consumed streaming body.
resolution.correction: Observe the first stream POST after preparation and apply the bounded preview deadline separately to the terminal outcome. Clone each actual browser response, match it to its request, and retain the verified request count through style and panel changes and reload.
resolution.prevention: Holding the real preparation for 3.4 seconds reproduces the former timeout. The clean final task run passed all eight replay and thirteen quality cases. It checks both paints against fixture prices, the frozen row, one accepted stream, explicit pre-admission BUSY and no additional subscription through reload.

items.source: Independent M1-001 review against the real three-symbol browser journey at b9778f7.
items.observation: An image change at completion and a count of successful replies could pass when a line missed its intermediate close or a failed subscription was followed by success. The single click-to-completion wait also combined real history preparation and stream service.

resolution.cause: The check observed all legend readings but only compared endpoint images. Its response filter ignored failed requests and its timer covered both operations.
resolution.correction: Track actual candle bodies and the line endpoint against independent fixture prices, classify every subscription attempt, and observe the stream POST before waiting for its terminal state.
resolution.prevention: The three-symbol test now distinguishes successive prices at the rendered scale and requires all intermediate and final draws, one accepted stream per selection, and explicit 429 BUSY for any preceding attempts. The clean task run also passed eight replay and thirteen quality cases.

items.source: Independent review and owned synthetic bridge probes at bebc1c2.
items.observation: Cropping the requested end by one millisecond hid an interior source gap. A replacement worker could change the volume of an earlier closed row under the same revision. A real worker exit during the repair read dropped the disconnection reason.

resolution.cause: Completion depended on repair eligibility, resume compared only the latest bar, and a failed repair read discarded the worker error.
resolution.correction: Track actual in-range gaps independently of repair, compare closed historical rows at the confirmed boundary, and preserve a worker failure after emitting the validated gap.
resolution.prevention: A one-millisecond crop, altered previously closed row and owned worker termination each have a regression. The ordinary chart retained the gap and the frozen history on a worker failure.

items.source: Independent follow-up review of 2d55f0a using the real provider and captured bridge frames.
items.observation: A same-hash replacement page declared a new visible gap while recovery still allowed completion. Altering the missing closed bar volume from 90 to 91 on an otherwise genuine repair frame retained its original digest and the chart accepted the altered value.

resolution.cause: The history row digest excludes quality coverage, and the consumer previously validated a repair digest only by its presence and format.
resolution.correction: Compare visible half-open gap coverage at the resume boundary. Verify the canonical digest of both received repair bars before projecting them after a completed stream.
resolution.prevention: The real worker probe stops before re-subscribing when visible coverage changes. An altered volume with its prior digest retains the gap and 39 frozen bars. Stopping or changing selection while verification is pending prevents late projection.

items.source: Hosted Windows Verify delivery run 44509534715, market-live-stream, first test after page reload.
items.observation: The five-second selected-bar assertion expired. The failure screenshot already shows the restored simulated futures chart, selected line style, open data window, forty bars and the original partial close of 3500.8 with volume 110. The other seven stream cases passed.

resolution.cause: The selected-bar assertion started before catalog and history had completed. Holding both real successful replies for 2.75 seconds each reproduced the Windows missing-element timeout with the original assertion.
resolution.correction: Observe every POST from issuance through the rendered chart, correlate completion or failure, and verify each read against its own deadline. Recheck the visible instrument, timeframe, chart style, simulated source and identical frozen final row after reload.
resolution.prevention: All eight replay cases pass with the bounded restore. Four independent negative probes reproduced the earlier false passes and confirm a failed extra read, an outstanding read, an unrelated BUSY and early history issuance are rejected.

items.source: Required Windows job 135536750939 at 9d1e403 in run 44517364634.
items.observation: Five Rust cases returned TIMEOUT during replacement verification or retry exhaustion. Ten repair-browser cases failed to observe their expected result under the default five-second assertion. The owned process interruption helper rejected its Windows launcher. The thirty-minute job ceiling cancelled the last suite before artifacts could be staged.

resolution.cause: Cold worker startup, browser progress assertions and process ownership on Windows exceeded assumptions from the Linux tests. The older hosted time budget also stopped artifact staging.
resolution.correction: Observe the real accepted worker and its confirmed cursor, verify each preparation and stream result, and isolate the test server from development watchers. Use the bounded Windows change job and retain its results.
resolution.prevention: Linux and Windows run 44542089017 independently passed Rust recovery and all 12 gap, 18 recovery UI, 13 quality, eight stream and one owned-process interruption cases. The Windows interruption test observed the real replacement and frozen bar.

items.source: Independent review of 59f0878 using synthetic futures rows, confined directories, valid long CSV fields and a partial output stream.
items.observation: A previous settlement price mapped to closing price without a diagnostic, and a source row marked open normalized as a closed bar. A shut down desktop host retained a readable selected directory. The parser rejected a valid field above its implicit library limit and skipped the next row. A short write could truncate a terminal result while the worker still reported success.

resolution.cause: The mapper accepted settlement aliases as OHLC and assumed source rows were closed. The reader inherited a smaller CSV field limit, its reply writer assumed a complete write, and shutdown did not close directory admission.
resolution.correction: Keep settlement fields independent from OHLC and require a closed source bar. Bound the CSV parser by the reviewed input size, drain framed writes, close admission and release owned workers and directory handles on shutdown.
resolution.prevention: Python, the Rust desktop registry and framed-worker regressions exercise prior settlement, open bars, a long multiline field followed by another bar, short writes and shutdown during preview.

items.source: Hosted Windows run 44524540362 and the reproduced Linux C-locale failure on the local folder branch.
items.observation: The architecture check read UTF-8 project source using the host default encoding and stopped before checking imports. This occurred on the Windows default code page when a provider contained a non-ASCII source label.

resolution.cause: The architecture scanner used the host text encoding to read UTF-8 source.
resolution.correction: Read the checked source explicitly as UTF-8.
resolution.prevention: The architecture regression contains non-ASCII source, and Windows also executes the repository architecture gate.

items.source: Native Windows report 44524484734 at 6a30e60 and genuine worker hello timings on the dedicated Windows 11 guest.
items.observation: The interrupted worker reached reconnecting and resumed, then returned TIMEOUT before the last confirmed bar. Two gap cases also timed out before a cold catalog and its following real history could present a chart. The prior core recovery and closed-bar repair checks passed in the same hosted run.

resolution.cause: An unused schema-format dependency compiled a grammar at each Python process start. Browser assertions also started before the cold catalog and history requests had completed.
resolution.correction: Keep the required format validators without the unused grammar, and observe successful catalog and history requests in order before checking the chart.
resolution.prevention: The same real Windows bridge recovered twice in about 2.17 seconds with the slimmer environment. Both hosted jobs in run 44542089017 passed the owned-worker, chart startup and schema format regressions.

items.source: GitHub Actions run 44536924867, hosted Linux dependency-review.
items.observation: The locked inventory passed. The approved live GitHub publisher advisory GET returned HTTP 403 with the anonymous REST rate limit exhausted, so dependency-review failed.

resolution.cause: The mandatory publisher advisory check shared the anonymous GitHub REST rate limit of the hosted runner.
resolution.correction: Fetch the one published advisory in an isolated step using the existing job credential at the exact approved TLS endpoint. The dependency checker validates fresh public metadata bound to that checkout, workflow attempt and runner.
resolution.prevention: Both jobs in run 44542089017 passed the isolated live fetch and online review of 540 locked packages and seven pinned actions. The regression suite covers refused redirects, stale records, unavailable advisories and credential isolation.

items.source: Real local-folder future preview under the merged minimal worker environment with no system IANA search path.
items.observation: A valid Asia/Shanghai night-session mapping produced timezone_unavailable and kept every record raw after an unrelated schema-format dependency stopped installing timezone data. The same mapping with the recorded IANA package restored its original UTC timestamp and explicit trading day.

resolution.cause: The local provider depended on incidental time-zone data supplied through an unrelated dependency.
resolution.correction: Pin tzdata as a direct requirement and resolve IANA time zones in the locked worker environment.
resolution.prevention: Run the night-session mapping without system tables and verify the independent UTC instant, reported trading day and rejection of ambiguous local times.

items.source: Independent checkpoint review of the opted-in local workspace at 9bb4647 with temporary synthetic profiles.
items.observation: The Vite launcher granted access based on loopback and origin without verifying possession of an owner-only launch credential. With a generally traversable POSIX profile root, database and journal sidecars used broad permissions. A second writer could commit a new workspace revision while the first launcher kept returning its startup snapshot to fresh clients.

resolution.cause: The launcher treated loopback origin validation as caller authentication and reused the startup snapshot. The store did not enforce a private profile root and private SQLite files before opening storage.
resolution.correction: Require a per-launch capability issued only through the verified private profile. Validate profile roots and SQLite files in the store. Read current state and eligible undo from Rust for every authorized snapshot.
resolution.prevention: Hosted run 44543693795 passed workspace-timeframe and rust-contracts-workers on Ubuntu and Windows. The browser cases reject anonymous and expired grants, observe a second writer's commit, and recover from stale context. The native controls verify profile binding, private database and sidecars, restart, replay and scoped undo.

items.source: Independent foreground terminal and same-port relaunch review of 081c59b.
items.observation: A terminal interrupt stopped both Vite and its writer. The private handoff file remained on disk even though the replacement launcher correctly denied its old authority. The Windows regular-file assertion also required a user SID even when a private inheriting ACL permits the elevated token default owner.

resolution.cause: The foreground SIGINT path could exit before Vite's close hooks ran. The original Windows file-owner assertion also assumed a single owner SID for a regular file even when an elevated token can supply an allowed default owner.
resolution.correction: Await Vite shutdown on terminal interrupt so the workspace close hook revokes the capability, removes the handoff and closes the writer. Require the current SID to own the profile directory and verify the regular file's allowed owner, inherited ACL and effective access independently.
resolution.prevention: Hosted Ubuntu workspace-timeframe passed the owned CLI SIGINT and SIGTERM case with file removal, writer exit and same-port relaunch. The Windows report separately records the expected POSIX signal skip. Its private handoff case passed, including inherited and effective access checks.

items.source: Hosted Windows run 44520641312 at 081c59b and the same native storage admission on a clean Windows 11 Enterprise 26H2 guest under a standard local account.
items.observation: All five hosted browser workspace cases and three native desktop tests failed while preparing the private profile. On Windows 11 build 26300.9457, both AppLocalData and the real 8.3 TEMP alias failed. Native ACL APIs returned the owner and DACL at every ancestor. The helper instead raised an InvalidCastException while evaluating an ancestor ACE. Five of six native storage library tests failed at ccb9f81.

resolution.cause: The guest reproduced an InvalidCastException in Windows PowerShell 5.1 when an ancestor ACE flags enum was evaluated with a bitwise mask. Native ACL reads returned the owner and DACL for both normal and short path spellings.
resolution.correction: Convert ACE flags, access values and comparison masks to integers before bitwise evaluation. Continue to require the current SID and inheritable private rights on the profile root and reject unsafe ancestors, SQLite files and sidecars.
resolution.prevention: Hosted Windows rust-contracts-workers passed all seven persistence library tests, including ancestor ACL admission and denial, TEMP alias equivalence and private inheritance with shared-root and sidecar denial. All six native desktop library tests passed, including absent AppLocalData provisioning. The Windows 11 guest also verified private startup and the alias path. These results cover hosted and virtualized Windows.

items.source: Synthetic Rust-process review of 89401c9 and independent rerun at 5453889c7e9029c6e80b23612a841abf2c38a9f4, stage_after_peer_deletion in .reports/decision-note-independent-5453889/coordinator-rust.json. The 5453889 decision-note-lifecycle log is in .reports/runs/20261119T133002.616158Z-22e48663/.
items.observation: Staging a missing later outcome copied the existing original note body. A second writer deleted the note and the first writer observed the new revision, but the first process retained the redundant staged payload. Expired payloads were collected only during later mutations. At 5453889, the regression asserted that an outcome-only stage held no original. The independent run observed one added outcome, zero added originals, and after the peer deletion at revision 2, zero live notes and one marker. Both old-stage decisions returned CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED and the detail returned DATA_UNAVAILABLE. Lifecycle regressions passed for observed revision invalidation, deadline expiry without another operation, and disposal.

resolution.cause: A pending outcome-only restore also retained an existing original. Collection depended on later mutations.
resolution.correction: Stage only missing content and release it on revision change, session disposal or expiry.
resolution.prevention: Storage tests exercise peer deletion, expiry and disposal. Independent decline and approve after supersession both require a new review.

items.source: Synthetic Rust-process review of 89401c9 and independent rerun at 5453889c7e9029c6e80b23612a841abf2c38a9f4, complete_backup_capacity in .reports/decision-note-independent-5453889/coordinator-rust.json. The 5453889 decision-note-lifecycle log is in .reports/runs/20261119T133002.616158Z-22e48663/.
items.observation: Two individually valid backups of the same note with 64 and 65 different later outcomes merged successfully. The resulting 129 outcomes were readable, but exporting the combined note failed with RESOURCE_LIMIT. At 5453889, both the independent run and the process regression observed RESOURCE_LIMIT before issuing a stage for the 129-outcome merge, with both archives unchanged. The 128-outcome boundary merged and exported every outcome, and the next append was rejected before approval with the complete export unchanged.

resolution.cause: Restore checked its input archive without checking the export size of the merged record.
resolution.correction: Validate the full resulting archive before staging and again before committing.
resolution.prevention: Two valid inputs with 64 and 65 outcomes are refused unchanged. The 128-outcome case round-trips exactly.

items.source: Synthetic Chromium review of 89401c9 and independent passing outcome_draft_after_peer_timeframe check at 5453889c7e9029c6e80b23612a841abf2c38a9f4 in .reports/decision-note-independent-5453889/coordinator-browser-draft.json. The 5453889 workspace-timeframe log is in .reports/runs/20261119T133002.616158Z-22e48663/.
items.observation: When a peer changed only the chart timeframe, a visible unsaved later-outcome draft and its date were silently discarded. At 5453889 the independent browser observed a fresh detail read after the peer changed 5m to 1d, preserved both draft fields, approved the outcome, and reopened it with the same text and date. The browser regression also passed for invalidating the older approval while keeping the draft and clearing the draft when its note was deleted.

resolution.cause: Refreshing a note after an unrelated workspace edit reset the local outcome form.
resolution.correction: Track the editable draft independently of refreshed note details and expire superseded approvals.
resolution.prevention: The two-window browser case preserves the typed date and result, saves the outcome and reopens it after a peer timeframe change.

items.source: Synthetic Chromium review of 89401c9 and independent rerun at 5453889c7e9029c6e80b23612a841abf2c38a9f4, deleted_index_rows_and_raced_open in .reports/decision-note-independent-5453889/coordinator-browser-list.json. The 5453889 workspace-timeframe log is in .reports/runs/20261119T133002.616158Z-22e48663/.
items.observation: After a peer deleted a note, a focused list still displayed its date and identity suffix across two polling intervals and after clicking the stale entry returned unavailable. At 5453889 the independent browser and workspace regression observed focus refresh removing the deleted entry and retaining the unrelated entry. A detail read that raced a second deletion returned DATA_UNAVAILABLE, and the list removed the stale entry and showed the empty state.

resolution.cause: The list retained an old note summary after the underlying note was deleted.
resolution.correction: Revalidate the focused list and retire an entry when its detail becomes unavailable.
resolution.prevention: The independent list and raced-detail cases remove only the deleted item. The integrated workspace browser repeats the case with separate writers.

items.source: Independent trusted Rust desktop dispatcher observation at 6c2f1a4 using only a temporary synthetic CSV and profile.
items.observation: The trusted dispatcher displayed a synthetic close of 5 using Close. Saving the same file digest and mapping revision with AltClose without an AltClose preview committed it. A restarted workspace loaded the unreviewed mapping, which normalized the same row to 6.

resolution.cause: Saving reran a private preview without establishing that the same mapping had already been presented through the public preview operation.
resolution.correction: Bind a successful public preview to the selected file, source digest, mapping and effective sample limit. Recheck the live selection and bytes before saving.
resolution.prevention: The registry rejects an unseen alternate close column. A separately previewed alternate saves and reopens at its own mapping revision.

items.source: Independent trusted Rust desktop dispatcher observation at 6c2f1a4 using only a temporary synthetic CSV and profile.
items.observation: A synthetic file kept identical decoded header bytes while an invalid UTF-8 byte in a later data row changed the complete checksum. Loading a reviewed mapping returned review_required and hid the record, the same response as an actual changed header.

resolution.cause: Header identity depended on decoding the entire file, conflating a bad later record with a changed header.
resolution.correction: Decode and compare the complete logical header independently. Return a distinct diagnostic when the header cannot be verified and report later decoding failures during full preview.
resolution.prevention: Tests distinguish unchanged headers followed by invalid bytes from changed, reordered, incomplete and undecodable headers and verify the whole-file digest.

items.source: Hosted Windows workspace-timeframe on a temporary synthetic profile.
items.observation: Hosted Windows run 44528913523 at 4a379d8 returned HTTP 200 for a synthetic workspace file check. The check captured status alone, so the returned representation is unknown. It could not distinguish the ordinary HTML fallback from a file response.

resolution.cause: Workspace-private paths lacked an explicit response before Vite's static handlers and SPA fallback. A raw path miss could return the application shell. The historical status-only result leaves the response body undetermined.
resolution.correction: Reject reserved workspace file names and direct raw filesystem URLs inside the bound private profile before Vite static serving or SPA fallback. Return an empty 404 with no-store and keep the private profile outside the served roots.
resolution.prevention: Hosted workspace-timeframe passed on Ubuntu and Windows. HEAD requests distinguish the ordinary HTML 200 fallback from the empty 404 with no-store for real synthetic SQLite, named sidecars, an ordinary file in the isolated profile and handoff paths.

items.source: Hosted Windows workspace-timeframe on a temporary synthetic profile.
items.observation: The independent file-permission check exited at an unspecified stage on Windows PowerShell 5.1 in hosted run 44528913523. It used enum operands in bitwise tests. The production workspace could already create a private profile and restore eligible undo on that runner.

resolution.cause: The original Windows assertion used enum operands in PowerShell 5.1 bitwise tests. A later hosted exit 52 combined provider lookup, descriptor read and owner comparison into one stage. A standard-user Windows 11 guest returned the current owner and DACL through both readers in both TEMP spellings, so the precise cause of that hosted exit remains undetermined.
resolution.correction: Use integer masks and explicitly read the owner and access sections through filesystem APIs. Report descriptor reads independently from owner mismatches. Keep the current-SID directory rule, allowed file owners and trustees, inherited rights and an actual read/write handle.
resolution.prevention: The Windows 11 guest passed the revised positive check in both TEMP spellings and reached the intended denial for broad access and missing inheritance on empty synthetic files. Hosted Windows workspace-timeframe at 290bd578 passed the same private handoff case with both negative controls.

items.source: PR 12 hosted Windows run 44531620190, market-workflow and ubuntu-preview logs.
items.observation: The three-symbol journey did not find Play sample updates within five seconds. The desktop, narrow-screen, and Retry demo preview paths hit the same five-second limit waiting for the first history chart. The assertions did not distinguish catalog latency, history latency, and rendering.

resolution.cause: One five-second browser assertion covered two serial worker reads and the first chart render. Holding each real reply reproduced startup beyond that assertion's budget.
resolution.correction: The shared startup verifier checks the real catalog request and reply, then the scoped history request and reply, before waiting for chart readiness. The preview suite exercises each held reply and a typed worker rejection. Product worker deadlines and retry behavior remain unchanged.
resolution.prevention: Hosted run 44544324678 for PR head cd93f96d076b0b7f0fa45374c646dfa463e199e3 passed market-workflow (1 case) and ubuntu-preview (7 cases) on Linux and Windows. The preview cases covered independently delayed catalog and history replies, offline Retry demo and a real worker rejection. Both task receipts retain their platform and log digests.

items.source: Synthetic published CSV and private Rust registry regression at cecda1c80829d42b7a120aba9ab4e3e12221669b. The observed red log is .reports/operations-workflow/cecda1c-red.log.
items.observation: The real shared selection advanced to interval A at selection revision 1 while the workspace revision stayed 0. An authenticated generic AI command using those revisions committed the main-chart timeframe at workspace revision 1 despite missing the selected interval's local analysis grant. The operations-workflow regression now requires a denial with no operation or replay row. A separately authorized on-device intent for B can commit through the same registry.

resolution.cause: The generic registry path accepted an AI timeframe intent before checking the current selection-specific on-device grant.
resolution.correction: Bind the operation to both workspace and selection revisions, then verify the current target and permitted analysis purpose for writes and receipt disclosure.
resolution.prevention: The SQLite operation workflow proves denied AI access makes no operation or replay record, concurrent retries commit once, and revocation blocks subsequent disclosure.

items.source: Windows 11 native MSVC/WebView2 engineering run on 2f4a0c0 with a selected synthetic 292-byte CSV, followed by two bounded standalone worker comparisons on the same guest.
items.observation: The actual desktop showed the complete digest after reading three raw rows in 2.17 seconds. The first native OHLCV preview subsequently displayed a worker timeout. The same worker exchange run directly twice returned closes 102 and 105, the incomplete-row diagnostic and process exit in 219 ms each. The native save and restart journey remains pending at this observation.

resolution.cause: The first native timeout did not expose its internal stage and later exact-source traces completed. The previous read-only worker exchange had no recovery after a genuine elapsed attempt.
resolution.correction: Permit one bounded replacement for a qualified read-only preview after confirmed cleanup, fresh authorization and cancellation checks. Reuse the frozen input and mapping. Preserve decoded terminal errors. ADR 0013 records interpreter ownership.
resolution.prevention: Controlled Linux and Windows runs verify worker identity, cleanup, cancellation, terminal errors and a successful replacement. Subsequent native raw and normalized previews, explicit save and restart completed. The cause of the original timeout remains undetermined.

items.source: Independent synthetic native Rust dispatcher replays at 4571353. The archive manifest identifies the original replay.json and events.jsonl observations. See archives/private/M0-039/historical-feedback-observations/local-csv-mapping-save-and-publication-replay/manifest.json.
items.observation: Replaying the same trusted mapping save with its original request ID, live folder and file, full digest, mapping and preview limit advanced the review revision from 2 to 3. A delayed retry of the already committed publication then returned STALE_CONTEXT. Publishing under revision 3 created a second dataset UUID with the same source and mapping digests, 504 identical bars and 506 source locators. A fresh one-row repro left two reviewed mapping versions, two byte-equivalent frozen revisions and one source blob. Independent lock tests preserved cancellation and changed-source rollback.

resolution.cause: A repeated committed save advanced the mapping revision and invalidated replay of its earlier publication.
resolution.correction: Reuse the current equivalent review and return exact admitted receipts under the current native grant and display right. Preserve fresh A-to-B-to-A mapping changes as separate versions.
resolution.prevention: The save, publish and lost-reply sequence retains one review, revision and original. Separate tests cover changed inputs, revoked rights and cancellation while a SQLite write waits.

items.source: Hosted Windows run 44548543796 at e960fd1, rust-contracts-workers log, and the native Win11 MSVC comparison at 2f4a0c0 retained in .reports/guest/2f4a0c0-mapping-path-reopen.
items.observation: The hosted restart test saved through a canonicalized synthetic directory and reselected the same source through the supplied spelling. Loading returned not_saved instead of saved before header comparison. On the Win11 guest, the same unmodified test and NTFS temporary directory passed with the long TEMP name and failed with its real 8.3 alias. The ordinary Win11 GUI observation with its selection spelling remains separately recorded.

resolution.cause: A path-derived association could differ across equivalent Windows long and short spellings of the same selected root.
resolution.correction: Resolve and verify native source association against the selected directory and retain compatibility with reviewed v4 keys.
resolution.prevention: Native MSVC cases cover long and actual 8.3 selection, restart, legacy v4 lookup, different directories containing the same bytes and a rejected junction.

items.source: Hosted Windows run 44563163301 rust-contracts-workers and independent standard-user Win11 MSVC measurements in .reports/windows-source-sharing/measured/CHANGES.JSON and PINS.JSON. The native Windows follow-up at 875f5e0 is recorded in contracts/reviews/2026-11-19-windows-folder-refresh-source-handles.json.
items.observation: The native bridge replay tests failed at bridge_tests.rs:523 and :608 with Win32 error 32. The independent desktop matrix reproduced error 32 for direct-child rename and atomic replacement after selection, preview and publication. Both succeeded before selection and after exit. The isolated handle matrix reproduced the failure with read-only sharing on the selected directory and distinguished that from the expected protection of a file currently being verified.

resolution.cause: The selected directory held restrictive sharing flags even while idle. Ordinary external saves and file replacements could then fail.

items.source: Owner storage review and repository-scoped allocated-block inventory on 2026-11-20.
items.observation: Across 45 existing worktrees, Cargo target directories occupied approximately 178.4 GiB of 194.8 GiB measured. Repeated local builds had no repository-wide retention budget.

resolution.cause: Each development worktree accumulated independent Cargo debug outputs. Completed incremental sessions and old dependencies or test executables continued occupying physical blocks after verification.
resolution.correction: Inventory repository-owned caches, collect positively identified idle artifacts above the budget, and default ordinary local verification to non-incremental builds. On the affected host Cargo outputs fell from 178.44 GiB to 81.05 GiB. A user timer runs the same pinned collector for checkouts on older revisions.
resolution.prevention: Regression fixtures cover non-destructive reporting, occupied files and executables, repository boundaries, threshold behavior and Cargo rebuilding after interruption. All 45 original Git heads and status snapshots, metadata for 31,290 retained evidence or diagnostic files, and 10,803 file digests matched after both sweeps. Active and unclassified artifacts can keep usage above the soft budget.

items.source: Owner review and registered worktree inventory on 2026-11-20.
items.observation: The projects directory contained the ScopeHub primary checkout and 43 sibling task worktrees. Shared storage maintenance only recognized the primary checkout directory, and retained build archives occupied the same source filesystem.

resolution.cause: Parallel and historical checkouts were created as project-directory siblings. The previous collector only admitted siblings, and generated runtime shims held absolute checkout paths.
resolution.correction: Provide a shared repository-local managed root and portable creation or reuse commands. On the affected host, move 36 idle checkouts, defer seven live sessions, retain three observed legacy mappings, and place the verified historical build archive on its optional volume. Ordinary source and build workflows remain on the source filesystem.
resolution.prevention: Regression tests cover repository identity, explicit branch and base, reuse, interruptions and storage eligibility. All 43 original worktrees matched Git and retained evidence after relocation. Host verification exercised the actual client build, four Rust/Python handshake cases, fresh worktree creation, Herdr routing, and an offline cache fallback. Process-death tests exercise kernel-released creation locks, including a Git child which outlives the launcher. The installed host alias resumed after a forced process exit.

items.source: PR 25 review and disposable native Git reproductions.
items.observation: The worktree helper accepted a Git file borrowed from a sibling linked checkout on the same branch. It also accepted a copied Git directory outside the native registry when its common directory, backlink and branch matched. New checkout creation reported success after a native hook switched HEAD to another branch.

resolution.cause: Several checkouts share the same Git common directory. The previous verification trusted the top level and shared metadata, and a successful native add did not prove the requested branch survived the checkout hook.
resolution.correction: Require a unique registration, the checkout-specific directory in the common worktree registry, its backlink to the checkout Git file, and the current symbolic branch. Recheck the requested branch after a native add.
resolution.prevention: Disposable native Git fixtures cover a borrowed Git file from the same branch, copied metadata, a branch-changing hook, detached relative registrations, and the standalone pinned host helper. The Ubuntu and Windows task runs pass these fixtures.

items.source: PR 25 review and disposable native Git and Cargo cache reproductions.
items.observation: Storage inventory admitted a managed root nested in a foreign Git checkout that the worktree manager would reject. When a foreign repository appeared after inventory, collection deleted a fixture artifact under the foreign checkout. The legacy sibling rule also permitted that nesting. Re-review reproduced both worktree creation and collection under a foreign .git file that Git could not resolve, including collection of an enclosing repository's tracked file after Cargo locks had been acquired. The existing M0-030 fixture additionally caught a change to the mounted-worktree diagnostic while combining the root and cache handle safeguards.

resolution.cause: Storage used a narrower ancestry check than the worktree manager. Git used exit 128 for both an empty marker directory and unresolved foreign metadata, which both callers could interpret as permission to proceed.
resolution.correction: Check foreign and unresolved ancestor Git markers at admission and under Cargo locks. Preserve mounted-worktree diagnostics and keep both host helpers independently runnable.
resolution.prevention: Independent disposable repositories exercise foreign linked ancestry, missing marker targets, and an outer Git repository’s committed file surviving collection after the locks. The existing mount and relocation fixtures continue to pass.

items.source: Independent reviews of PR 24 at 98506a29aa50f82f9ff8b08417a3323d2949aa41, cbab3a9ec47a3c2611fcdebeafa46717dad7cc6f and 001dcd753ef31ca3a244cf058dff955134938a1a, and disposable M0-033 regression fixtures.
items.observation: The Linux process scan skipped other UIDs, allowing removal without a lease while a foreign process could be holding a dependency open. Collection accepted replacements at inventoried child cache paths, including changed debug directories and absent, replaced or edited .rustc_info.json markers. The first repair compared indistinguishable directory stat samples on filesystems with coarse timestamps and inode reuse. The live-handle repair protected those caches, then a review with RLIMIT_NOFILE=32 found descriptor exhaustion prevented all nine revalidations and was reported as an identity change. A regular file at target raised NotADirectoryError during child discovery and interrupted the repository-wide review.

resolution.cause: The process audit skipped processes by UID. Cache admission used directory names and then sampled inode metadata as proof. Retained handles could exhaust the descriptors required by revalidation. Child discovery also assumed that every target entry was a directory.
resolution.correction: Observe all visible processes and use the partial-visibility policy whenever one cannot be observed. Bind guarded observations to live directory handles and revalidate fresh paths and Cargo provenance under the locks. Reserve transient descriptors and report resource-limited candidates. Inventory ordinary target files without attempting child discovery.
resolution.prevention: Disposable fixtures reproduce held foreign dependencies, replacements with indistinguishable sampled metadata, changed child markers, ordinary files and resource pressure at RLIMIT_NOFILE=32. The offline Cargo fixture verifies a group interruption, retained files and rebuilding. The exact functional head passed local verification and the Linux and Windows jobs in run 44889925831.

items.source: Owner worktree review and separate read-only reproductions by the development supervisor during M0-031 on 2026-11-21.
items.observation: The owner identified that M4-001 referenced its blocked diagnostic through another checkout and requested criteria for worktree retirement. Moving or retiring that checkout could make the diagnostic unavailable. During implementation the development supervisor reproduced two false retirement candidates in temporary Git worktrees. One still supplied a report to a committed operational script in another checkout. The other appeared to retain its only diagnostic because an archive root above the checkout resolved back to the original file.

resolution.cause: The report dependency used a checkout location as its identity. The initial retirement observation did not cover operational script consumers and could resolve a claimed archive copy inside the checkout it was evaluating.
resolution.correction: Record portable diagnostic locators and reject nonlocal report paths in active and newly reviewed records and operational scripts. Keep archive reads explicit and verify original report bytes and associated files. Hold worktrees when a downstream consumer exists, retention is unverified, or an observation is incomplete.
resolution.prevention: M0-031's recorded Linux checks passed positive and negative Git fixtures, including tracked and untracked script consumers, an overlapping archive root, an archive symlink back into the checkout, independent retained copies and incomplete activity visibility. The actual host report held all 50 registrations, including 10 tips reachable from the observed origin/main. Explicit resolution of the M4 diagnostic verified 13 logs and the archive checksum manifest and preserved the blocked outcome with 13 selected checks passed and two blocked.

items.source: Independent Herdr reviews of PR 27 and read-only host observations on 2026-11-21, plus authenticated failed Ubuntu and Windows runs 44887586115 and 44891186224 now verified in the permanent development archive.
items.observation: Independent fixtures exposed missed check registry, live symlink, editable Python and Cargo build output dependencies, lost worktree-private Git recovery references, incomplete observation artifact verification, caller-relative and exported report regressions, and an unused clean filter holding idle checkouts. Hosted Python checks failed on both platforms under globally configured Git LFS. Windows also missed untracked and ignored symlinks and rejected an independent archived file. The supervisor reproduced cross-checkout diagnostic paths escaping history checks in app, workflow and crate sources and requested a human review intake for the otherwise clear checkouts affected only by partial process visibility. A read-only inventory of the integrated PR 21 checkout showed that six standard scoped pnpm links were treated as unretained files despite resolving to its own locked virtual store. Follow-up reviews reproduced false candidates from nested Cargo paths with and without dot components, a linked harness registry and a sole diagnostic under Cargo deps. They found nonlocal report references accepted in HTML, SQL and harness commands and a manually placed root pnpm link misclassified as rebuildable. The first exact native Windows retry passed the original LFS, symlink and archive cases, and exposed duplicate attribution of one editable Python path through case-insensitive Lib and lib aliases.

resolution.cause: The original observation relied on directory classifications, incomplete path and Git state enumeration, and configured rather than effective clean filters. Report selection and verification also omitted established caller and artifact bindings. The first corrected Windows run exposed a second spelling for the same virtual environment library directory.
resolution.correction: Verify declaring runtime paths, worktree-private object recovery, scoped pnpm placement and Cargo output ownership. Read editable libraries from actual directory entries, observe effective filters with external drivers disabled, restore caller-relative and independent report imports, and verify bound field and session artifacts. Surface human review intake while preserving the sole partial-process hold.
resolution.prevention: Local and hosted task verification matched the clean 320946e execution inputs. Ubuntu ran 438 Python tests and Windows ran the same suite with 45 platform skips. The stable host read-only snapshot found two intake rows and zero candidates among 50 registrations. One intake row verified 17 retained files, while the integrated product checkout verified 999 and remained held for additional unarchived files. The three failure reports retain their original failed outcomes and verified manifests. The retained M4 run still records 13 passed checks and two blocked.

items.observation: Two Vite synthetic history fixtures and their workspace writers survived for hours after their original owner exited. They held two listening ports and a historical checkout, with no connected clients. Ordinary termination of the two verified fixture parents released both listeners and their writers.

resolution.cause: The synthetic workspace preview listened for an explicit IPC close message. Exiting its parent closed the IPC channel without requesting the Vite shutdown that reaps the real workspace writer.
resolution.correction: The IPC fixture observes disconnect before Vite setup and serializes shutdown with startup. Explicit close and IPC loss release a held response, close the Vite server and its writer, and disconnect IPC only while connected.
resolution.prevention: The workspace-timeframe check exercises an established writer, a held response, startup disconnect and duplicate close. The final native Linux and Windows task artifacts bind the exact source and regression observations. An independent process-level comparison on Linux confirmed a real parent exit leaked the listener and writer at the integrated baseline and released both at the corrected source.

items.source: Main workflow 44906026863, native Windows job 136851666782, artifact 14709052375, ZIP SHA-256 7a6997e80910061bc0299139d6638a009d3ec9bfe763771f410c5f4e366f3531. The same product tree passed PR workflow 44902878648.
items.observation: At workspace.spec.mjs line 980, the eight-second wait for workspace revision 2 expired. The retained browser image shows a successful removal message, the previous disabled accepted layer and a busy workspace. The embedded removal-stage attachment did not record a completed snapshot.

resolution.cause: A committed indicator change refreshed the workspace through a one-shot snapshot. A genuine admission refusal left the old view and a persistent busy state even after the writer was available. In the unmodified product, the eight-second observer expired while an independent authorized read returned the correct stored layer state and undo.
resolution.correction: After an indicator commit, compare the authoritative snapshot with the receipt's workspace and minimum revision. Retry only eligible, side-effect-free snapshot reads within a four-second retry-start budget, cancel on view teardown and queue the read behind an active workspace operation. Each admitted request keeps its original transport deadline.
resolution.prevention: The real frozen-chart regression retains its eight-second observation, forces a true first-read HTTP 429 and validates persistent remove and undo counts, request identities and the recovered workspace. Local targeted negative checks also cover non-retryable BUSY, terminal cancellation, wrong workspace, lagging revision and teardown during backoff for both buttons. The selected market-worker checks and both hosted jobs in 44913291282 passed.

items.source: Native Windows M4-006 workflow 44919188381 attempt 1 on 46bcadea3338c3fadd54f2c25b45847fdb18a96a. The retained model-connection-workflow log SHA-256 is aa7055f346c43f6a738c126a228d8b5374e05b47d0a480928c885d902a4f628a.
items.observation: Only case 7 of 10, one scoped activation delivers two ordinary turns to the owned peer and handles denial, failure and cancellation, failed. Playwright reported route.continue: Route is already handled! at tests/ui/ai-workflow-fixture.mjs:149. A local Chromium reproduction holds a same-origin request in a context observer after page fallback. Removing the final matching page route lets the driver resolve the request, then a later legacy context-wide continue throws. The origin-filtered comparison delivered one local request and blocked the separate synthetic origin without a route error.

resolution.cause: A page handler fell back to a context observer that held a same-origin request. Removing the final matching page route let Playwright resolve the request while the observer was still active. When the observer fell back, the legacy context-wide guard tried to continue the resolved route and Playwright rejected the duplicate terminal action.
resolution.correction: Match only browser requests whose origin differs from the exact preview origin. Record and abort each matched request and fail the assertion if any were recorded. Same-origin requests stay with normal browser handling or an explicit page fault.
resolution.prevention: The registered Chromium regression holds the observer through route removal, observes one local service arrival and verifies that an attempted second loopback origin has zero arrivals and fails the guard assertion. It reproduced the legacy error three times and passed three times with the repair. The full browser workflow and Rust replay passed locally and on authenticated Ubuntu and native Windows workflow 44923738119 attempt 1 at f7a0e469b1e106ff964f07b614deb3ae4c963bc5.

items.source: GitHub Actions M4-006 run 44926633907 and the independent controlled Chromium reproduction recorded on PR 23.
items.observation: A periodic published-revision status read can hold the local admission slot when the user selects a source. A rejected foreground request left the dialog open and the independently observed database unchanged.

resolution.cause: The published revision watcher held the preview writer admission slot. The source click discarded a definite BUSY refusal and did a one-shot snapshot after any accepted write. At fc6e88a the independent Chromium fixture held a real Rust status reply. The foreground received HTTP 429, the source and selection revision stayed unchanged in SQLite and the dialog remained open. The original hosted log pins the visible symptom.
resolution.correction: Pause background revision checks during the foreground source operation. Reuse its original request and revision only after a definite refusal. Verify acknowledged writes against an authoritative snapshot, preserve a newer selection and expose read-only recovery after a missing acknowledgement. An admitted write settles independently of closing the dialog. Closing the dialog cancels any unadmitted retry.
resolution.prevention: All seven synthetic cases passed three consecutive local Chromium runs. Ubuntu and Windows passed both hosted task selections at ad7037f03c10b683928b247a655be22cf0a46dfa in runs 44973437972 and 44973438056. The registered regression observes actual status and mutation results, counts accepted writes, and checks the UI, SQLite state and an independent registry snapshot. The local baseline and repeated pass reports are retained with SHA-256 43c64662a8b696c79cb497e301b17ef5bdcdcd6016d5ff6b85f30fc6d5ad9c22 and af55964d22869646f7ad3bce934a62278f0e74cc3a45eb701a09739fb1e61dd8.

items.source: Independent Chromium and Rust writer review of PR 23 at 69997fdf24e14417e62369a6e658ae0939631983.
items.observation: The real writer accepted one frozen source selection at revision 1. When the browser response was withheld after commit and the dialog was closed, the workspace still showed No data source and Checking workspace source after 17.5 seconds. No recovery action was available. An independent snapshot confirmed the persisted frozen source and releasing the response restored the chart.

resolution.cause: The source admission budget controlled when to retry a definite refusal. An issued browser reply or native invoke could keep the source operation pending indefinitely. The owner-provided synthetic script reproduced both held-response stages at 69997fd with one accepted write, durable frozen revision 1 and no recovery action after 17.5 seconds.
resolution.correction: Give each issued source write and readback a separate 15-second response deadline on both transports. Observe an expired write as uncertain and perform read-only reconciliation. Ignore late results. An outstanding native write retains its recovery guard until independently fenced by a newer revision or followed by a snapshot taken after transport settlement.
resolution.prevention: The nine browser source cases and the desktop IPC regression passed locally. Both hosted task selections passed on Ubuntu and Windows at ad7037f03c10b683928b247a655be22cf0a46dfa in runs 44973437972 and 44973438056. The cases hold genuine committed responses, verify the recovery action, commit a competing revision and deliver the stale result after recovery. The desktop fixture substitutes IPC delivery and uses the real Rust registry. Independent review repeated both timed-out response stages and both peer revision scenarios on the exact hosted source. The retained clean browser comparison reports have SHA-256 c14d2e898f1ae9a0d60acdb286176a4df2a740aaef1fdcdf7f87bed21bfee517 and aa8911dc710f099fcd11d163990c20f2acffbca6a809ddae69ce62602b9b18cf.

A delayed evaluation after load and an independent HTTP 503 both produced that assertion. The original Windows screenshot locates the symptom before mount, and its exact trigger remains undetermined.

The previous control and private-record disconnect assertions passed on Ubuntu and Windows in authenticated run 44977426468. The archived original report and screenshot were verified. The local comparison index has SHA-256 5c366dcc40ec1122a801baea615a7c15e37bcf8c3eaeca1c0fed956596406dbd.

items.source: Independent Chromium, Vite and Rust writer review using the actual private launcher on PR 31 at 3d26f0ead10da7ac08c1ed784eed1d8ccb1adcc0.
items.observation: An exception after imports and before React mount left the private grant consumed and the static Reload window control visible. Reload then opened the public shell without a private snapshot. An entry HTTP failure before grant consumption retained the fragment and ordinary reload restored the private workspace.

resolution.cause: The static recovery script offered Reload window independently of grant consumption. A real private launch consumed the fragment during module evaluation before a later exception could prevent React from mounting. Reload opened the public shell.
resolution.correction: Consuming a valid private grant hides and disables the static reload control and directs the user to reopen the original private access document. Public and pre-consumption failures still offer Reload window. The consumed grant remains in page memory.
resolution.prevention: Real file-launch navigation verified pre-consumption and public reload, post-consumption relaunch with an authorized Rust snapshot, and an inert refresh of the cleaned private page. items.source: Owner review and live GitHub branch and PR inventory on 2026-11-21.
items.observation: At main f7624a93 GitHub had 35 branch heads. Twenty-three non-default heads were reachable from main, and seven stacked pull requests remained open with their full heads already integrated. Six other backup heads required independent preservation and comparison.

resolution.cause: Task heads remained after verified merges. Superseded stacked pull requests and recoverable backup heads had no recurring reconciliation. Workflow selection also treated a shared head SHA as a sufficient pull request identity.
resolution.correction: Verified exact ancestry, dependent pull requests, recovery copies and original hosted evidence. Retired the 29 redundant remote heads and enabled automatic deletion on merge. Added live inventory and validation of the actual tested pull request, head and base.
resolution.prevention: Weekly branch and worktree reviews now surface through project status alongside a monthly compatibility review. Fixtures exercise fork name collisions, older recorded base tips, direct recovery refs, ambiguous runs and stale tested merge checkouts. Recheck live protection, expected tips, open dependents and independent recovery before retirement.

items.source: Independent review of PR 30 at 26aab9d with two required platform jobs.
items.observation: A successful Linux checkout supplied the source identity for the entire run. Both a missing and an obsolete Windows checkout incorrectly resulted in a ready recommendation in the two-job reproduction. A second replay showed that an older correct run could conceal a newer same-PR checkout with an incorrect head parent.

resolution.cause: The assessment read one checkout for the entire run and could skip a newer incorrect checkout as if only the base had changed.
resolution.correction: Verify the checkout of each protected required job and the exact two parents of its tested merge. Block a newer same-PR attempt with an incorrect head.
resolution.prevention: The regressions alter and remove the second checkout, and place a newer incorrect run ahead of a valid older one. Authentic Ubuntu and Windows logs exercise the successful pair.

resolution.correction: Expose an actionable finding and block the review when a stable snapshot reports the default unprotected. The weekly checklist invokes the full protection comparison.
resolution.prevention: Tests distinguish a protected default, ordinary unprotected feature branches, a protection change during observation and a stably unprotected default.

items.source: Authenticated main verification run 44993393461 at 32bb9671e78e2e0114ade28381d93c7e23f1a1cd. Original report and logs retained as archives/runs/20261122T062415.160535Z-d15c8a2c/test-report.json.
items.observation: On Windows, test_timeout_preserves_partial_diagnostics read the partial output and reported the timeout, then temporary directory cleanup failed twice with WinError 32 when removing fixture.log. The traceback does not identify who held the file.

resolution.cause: The Windows venv redirector could start the actual gated interpreter before assignment. The native control independently observed that interpreter outside the verification job. The original failure did not record the file holder, and a separate read handle reproduced the same error.
resolution.correction: Start the isolated standard-library gate with the base interpreter and assign that exact process before releasing it to launch the selected command. Preserve the command, partial diagnostics and strict cleanup failure reporting.
resolution.prevention: Windows run 44996898959 verified actual Job membership, the same live writer handle through timeout cleanup, native delete access before hashing, the retained bytes and digest, and strict deletion. The writer was still unsignaled just after job accounting drained and had exited when the full cleanup returned.

items.source: Authenticated PR 35 verification run 44997698442, head bd6233001b3874cb1fb843606663d32fa54edb4f and tested merge 8dcda240584f4115ed5e7560e386c3620c40ae77. Original report and logs retained as archives/runs/20261122T072140.708728Z-edfb023d/test-report.json.
items.observation: Only the new Windows timeout writer observation failed. Its process handle returned WAIT_TIMEOUT both after Job stop and at run_logged return, 0.250 seconds from the timed wait. The DELETE access probe succeeded. The original timeout log test and the redirector membership control passed.

resolution.cause: Job accounting removed terminating members before their process objects necessarily signaled. The cleanup waited on the launcher handle while the observed writer could still be terminating.
resolution.correction: Retain handles for confirmed Job members before requesting termination, join them under one deadline and keep the Job accounting guard. If inspection fails, attempt termination and wait for the already confirmed members under the same bound. Report both inspection and shutdown failures if both occur.
resolution.prevention: Native run 45000485659 confirmed actual live writer membership, exit at both cleanup boundaries, and intact, deletable diagnostics. Independent review exercised resize, membership and failure paths, including shared deadlines and compound errors. The confirmed snapshot is the scope of explicit member waits.

items.source: Desktop localization engineering review on 2026-11-22. A synthetic restored equity without a declared price tick reproduced the issue.

items.source: Authenticated Windows verification for main push 45018382994 and PR 41 run 45018440319. Original diagnostics are retained under archives/runs/20261122T114203.123694Z-afc7cc49/test-report.json and archives/runs/20261122T114251.223282Z-6c1990d5/test-report.json.
items.observation: Chromium reported ERR_NO_BUFFER_SPACE during same-origin Vite module loading in distinct workspace-timeframe cases in both Windows runs. The main push also failed desktop-localization navigation to its loopback listener. The Linux jobs passed.

resolution.cause: The pinned Playwright 1.64.0 launched Chromium 156 with Windows TCP source-port randomization active. Playwright issue 43545 links this path to intermittent Winsock 10055, including on loopback. Both original Windows reports match this failure. They contain no failure-time kernel trace, and an additional old-version run completed without reproducing the error.
resolution.correction: Pin the development runner and its Playwright dependencies to 1.65.1. The upstream change in microsoft/playwright#43605 disables TcpPortRandomizationWin in Chromium. Product binaries, OS settings, retries and protected check selection are unchanged.
resolution.prevention: The regression reads actual Chromium launch arguments through CDP and records the effective feature in desktop-localization.log. It failed with the old browser and passed with Chromium 159.0.8154.6. Hosted run 45023093160 passed workspace-timeframe, desktop-localization and the online dependency review on both platforms. Revisit the version-specific guard after an upstream fix or retirement of the affected path.

items.source: PR 41 run 45028387189, Ubuntu job 137226316277. Retained report at archives/runs/20261122T133800.124696Z-cdcf5ecd/test-report.json and adjacent verification-scope.json (SHA-256 324f3285ffc8b8440e13420088bc8a88dc2c25b57f9527340f8cfdb29bde4fe4).
items.observation: The full harness succeeded on the actual merge checkout, but selection recorded comparison_unavailable and no base or count. The selector log rejected the event merge SHA after validating the PR ref, checkout and both parents.
